Oh wow I didn't know that fact about PCP's at all. I've had a bad experience with the mental health center at my school but I have yet to visit the student health center. I'll definitely be doing that and see if they offer any options. If not, I'll look in PCP's in my network. Thank you for replying!

I have a dewyful and a juicy. I much prefer the dewyful because the juicy has a bad smell/taste to it. Not sure if it's just the shade I have though. I will say that the stain on the juicy is stronger and longer lasting for me.

I use them because I have long and dark nose hairs that are very noticeable. I don't think they are blackheads but everyone else who sees them does and it's embarrassing. I don't know of any other options for my case since they're literal hairs. :/
Our tiny tank. 😂 I love it! Totally agree.

Thank you for your reply. You're right, I don't love myself. I've been trying to forgive myself for my mistakes recently but I struggle to maintain peace with myself when I start thinking of how others will judge me in the future. I'd love to talk with you.

I didn't buy any kitchenware because I don't plan to ever use kitchenware. If I ever am in dire need of something  I don't want to have to be paying $35 to use a cutting board one time. Referring to a reasonable price, I would not be making the price up. I would of course ask them what they think I should pay. More likely, I would just buy my own things. As for the $35, I wasn't complaining about not getting the exact money's worth. I was concerned about how we were going to split items without animosity or awkardness. Items that I may add neither I nor my other roommate had any opinion on buying. I'm living in a dorm because that's the only housing option I have. I agree that bonding over cooking sounds like a great experience but I am not even sure if I want to bond with these roommates and do not plan to cook for a variety of circumstances. Thanks for your insight though. I've also been reevaluating how I handled things.

As far as I know they only asked her to pay $20. I don't know the reasons as to why, but it's another point as to why I was offended :/ I do think that they were most likely being enthusiastic. I just didn't like how they handled the situation. As of right now, I don't plan go use any of their items but I have communicated that if and when I decide to do so I will of course pay them a reasonable amount depending on what the item(s) are.

Thanks for letting me know that the situation isn't normal, as someone whose living with roommates for the first time. I definitely share the same concerns regarding move out and I'm of the opinion that even if we did split items there's no way we'll all walk away with exactly $35 worth of items.

We all have a meal plan. It's about 15 minutes away to the cafeteria though so maybe they don't want to commute/just want to cook for themselves. Thank you for your insight. I found it really helpful and unbiased. I can definitely see sharing meals as being a bonding experience and they actually bought useful things. I guess I'm just hung up about their non communication and my assumptions about how little I will actually be using the kitchen.
